rv.q: Outrageously funny Mindelle plays Celine as an omniscient narrator who gloriously upstage everybody else.
But eventually 'Titanique' comes into its own as it revs up into increasing absurdity
If you're not already a fan of the music and the movie, this mashup is unlikely to make you one.
The cast and creators' enthusiasm is infectious, and if you just let it wash over you, you'll have a boatload of fun.
“Titanique” delivers. It’s really funny. And it doesn’t matter that the film “Titanic” is celebrating its 25th anniversary this month.
'Titaníque' is a guaranteed good night out for anyone who lived through America's late-'90s Titanic phase.

Even if you have to beat a couple of Swedes in a portside game of poker for a ticket—and slum it in third-class—near, far, wherever you are, get yourself to New York’s Theatre to experience Titanique, a show so ridiculous that it is pure comedy genius.
Titanique is the most hilarious musical parody to play New York in many a year.
I had a great time on my Titanic crossing and I think you will, too.
As jokes land and jokes sink, there’s still the joy of hearing many of Dion’s greatest hits, a cavalcade of top-tier pop.
Titanique is a cheery diversion, and its fitting finale is the enthused audience singing along with Celine Dion.
The worst you can say about Titanique is that it is harmless; if people want to knock back Cosmopolitans and yuk it up at bad jokes, that's their business.
